scene.description: Outdoor residential exterior in warm Californian late-morning light. Subject occupies the left ~50% of the frame: an anonymous installer in warm casual workwear and tool belt, three-quarter-back-view, completing a finished window install — last shim, final sealant pass, stepping back to inspect, OR wiping hands clean. The freshly installed window is visible at the install point with its clean fresh-fabricated frame and divided-light or single-light glass clearly seated in the wall. NO face visible. Right ~50% of frame is occupied by a clean white rendered Google review card overlaying the same exterior background — IDENTICAL to V1 and V2. A circular 35 YEARS anniversary ribbon-seal sits in the bottom-left corner. A row of 5 yellow stars sits across the bottom-right above clean negative space where the CDW wordmark lockup will be composited in Canva post-generation — render that area as natural continuation of the surrounding exterior background, no placeholder box, no dashed outline, no white wordmark zone marker.
scene.subject: Anonymous installer (NO recognizable face). Three-quarter-back-view, completing a finished install. Workwear and tool belt visible. Body language reads as 'job done' — final inspection, hands dusted, clean step-back. The finished window is visible at the install point as an outcome cue.
scene.setting: Southern California residential exterior — wall around a freshly installed window, beige/stucco siding visible, no recognizable house number, no readable street sign, no specific neighborhood signage.
scene.action: Final-step / completion gesture — stepping back to inspect, wiping hands, final sealant pass, last shim, OR closing the window for the first time. Static / near-static. The framing shifts the moment from V2's mid-install to V3's just-finished.

style.primary: editorial outcome / finished-install documentary still — clones REF-001's installer-with-window composition; subject in completion mode, finished window visible as outcome cue
style.rendering_quality: hyperrealistic photographic, slight phone-photo realism, no Instagram filter, no luxury-mansion gloss
style.surface_textures: workwear fabric weave, tool-belt leather, fresh-fabricated window frame, clean glass surface, beige stucco siding, sealant bead at frame perimeter
style.lighting: natural late-morning Californian daylight ~5200K, warm cast — IDENTICAL to V1 and V2 lighting

camera.aperture: f/4 — subject and finished window in focus; review card on right remains crisp and readable
camera.angle: eye level, slightly off-axis to match REF-001's framing — angle subtly different from V2 to read as a different moment

technical.resolution: 1440x1800 mobile-first 4:5 vertical (Meta Feed / Reels / IG Feed)
technical.rendering: Editorial finish, real-photo authenticity, no heavy color grade. Warm Californian craft palette per CDW design system.

materials.skin: Hands visible if naturally framed; no facial features rendered (back-view or three-quarter-back-view). Avoid plastic AI skin on visible hands; avoid warped fingers.
materials.fabric: Long-sleeve work shirt in warm neutral (off-white, weathered red, or soft black per CDW palette). Standard work pants. Tool belt visible.
materials.surfaces: Fresh-fabricated window frame seated in opening; clean glass surface; sealant bead at frame perimeter; beige stucco siding.
materials.transparency: Window glass shows light reflection consistent with daylight scene; subtle reflection of installer's silhouette is acceptable; no jarring artificial highlights.

environment.atmosphere: Outdoor residential exterior; mid-to-upper-middle-class Southern California neighborhood feel.
environment.time: Late morning — warm but pre-noon shadow direction (matches V1 and V2).
environment.particles: Faint sun-warmed atmospheric haze acceptable; no dust storms, no smoke.

composition.perspective: Three-quarter-back-view of installer at left half — clones REF-001's framing; finished install visible as outcome cue.
composition.framing: Left ~50% installer-in-completion-gesture photo · Right ~50% rendered Google review card overlay. NO top logo strip. Circular 35 YEARS ribbon-seal in bottom-left corner. Row of 5 yellow stars across bottom-right above clean negative space where the CDW wordmark lockup will be composited in Canva post-generation — that area renders as natural continuation of the surrounding exterior background, no placeholder box, no dashed outline, no white wordmark zone marker. Frame extends full-bleed to bottom edge.
composition.subject_placement: Subject occupies left ~50%; back/torso mid-frame; arms extended toward window or held at chest height in inspection gesture; freshly installed window visible at install point.

spec.verbatim_review_body_preferred_full_text: We had doors replaced about 6 years ago by a 'virtual' outfit and it turned into constant repairs, service calls, and headaches once the warranty ended. This time we wanted a real local company... when you call, a real person picks up and gets things handled. No 'press 1, press 4, press 8' maze.
spec.truncation_fallback_if_needed: We had doors replaced about 6 years ago by a 'virtual' outfit and it turned into constant repairs... This time we wanted a real local company... when you call, a real person picks up and gets things handled. No 'press 1, press 4, press 8' maze.
spec.visual_focal_point_sentence: When you call, a real person picks up and gets things handled. No 'press 1, press 4, press 8' maze.
spec.focal_point_treatment: Visual hierarchy of the card should make the focal-point sentence the most readable focal point.
spec.verbatim_accuracy_lock: Path 2 verbatim accuracy lock — review body and reviewer details are EXACT, not paraphrased. If at generation time any rendered detail differs from spec, the variation FAILS Agent 9 review and must be regenerated.

review_card.anonymization_compliance: Display name 'San Diego homeowner' + neutral generic avatar circle (no letter, no initial) complies with the CDW Round 1 testimonial anonymization lock per system designer's finalized decision 2026-04-26. Real source reviewer on file is Zoran Knezevic; the displayed attribution does NOT carry his name, initials, or any identifying detail. Review body text remains verbatim.
